name: Georg Balthasar Ritter von Neumayer
summary: German geophysicist and geomagnetician known for polar research, navigation instruments, and magnetic charts.

name: Kirchheimbolanden
summary: Town in Rheinpfalz, Lower Palatinate, birthplace of Neumayer.

name: Polytechnikum in Munich
summary: Technical university in Munich where Neumayer studied civil engineering.

name: University of Munich
summary: University where Neumayer worked as an assistant after graduation.

name: Sternwarte Bogenhausen
summary: Astronomical observatory near Munich where Neumayer worked under Lamont.

name: Johann von Lamont
summary: Leading geomagnetician of the 19th century and Neumayer's tutor.

name: Flagstaff Observatory
summary: Observatory for navigation, meteorology, and terrestrial magnetism founded by Neumayer in Australia.

name: Royal Society of Victoria
summary: Scientific society in Victoria, Australia, where Neumayer served as Vice President.

name: Deutsche Seewarte
summary: National German institution for hydrography, meteorology, and maritime science directed by Neumayer.

name: Marineobservatorium Wilhelmshaven
summary: Imperial geomagnetic observatory established with Neumayer's help in Wilhelmshaven.

name: Carl Börgen
summary: Head of the Marineobservatorium Wilhelmshaven and Neumayer's collaborator.

name: International Polar Commission
summary: Organization coordinating the First Polar Year, presided over by Neumayer.

name: Adolf Schmidt
summary: Geomagnetician who modified Gaussian theory and succeeded Eschenhagen at Potsdam.

name: Berghaus' Physikalischer Atlas
summary: Atlas containing Neumayer's geomagnetic charts published in 1891.

name: Neustadt, Pfalz
summary: Town close to Neumayer's birthplace where he died.
